- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% if recent price is trending up.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); cap forecast increase after spike to 3–5% max.
- If 3+ consecutive days of high sentiment + price rise, model often fails to mean-revert; apply downward correction of 0.5–1.5% per day after peak.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate later periods (especially 15–30 days ahead) — reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% per 5-day horizon.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction — match forecast slope to sentiment trend, not historical mean.
